desc: Precompute prefix distinct counts: L[i] = number of distinct elements in A[0..i-1] (0-indexed).
Precompute suffix distinct counts: R[i] = number of distinct elements in A[i..N-1].

Use a segment tree to maintain values for each possible left split point i. As we iterate j from 1 to N-2 (0-indexed, so middle subarray ends at j, starts at some i+1), update the segment tree when a new element A[j] is encountered. Specifically, for each position k where A[j] last appeared, the distinct count for subarrays starting after k and ending at j will include A[j]. We need to carefully update the values.

Actually, a simpler O(N) approach exists: iterate the middle subarray's right boundary j. Maintain an array `best[i]` which represents L[i] + distinct(A[i+1..j]). When moving from j to j+1, for each i, distinct(A[i+1..j+1]) is distinct(A[i+1..j]) + (1 if A[j+1] not in A[i+1..j] else 0). The condition "A[j+1] not in A[i+1..j]" is equivalent to "the last occurrence of A[j+1] is before i+1", i.e., last_pos[A[j+1]] < i+1, i.e., i > last_pos[A[j+1]]. So for all i > last_pos[A[j+1]], the value increases by 1. We can use a segment tree with range add and range max to maintain these values.

Initialize the segment tree with L[i] for i from 0 to N-2 (since i can be from 0 to N-2, and j from i+1 to N-2, with the last subarray starting at j+1 <= N-1). For j=1 (0-indexed, so middle subarray is A[1..1] if i=0), we start with j=1. For each j from 1 to N-2, we update the segment tree: add 1 to all positions i in range [last_pos[A[j]] + 1, j-1] (since i must be < j, and i > last_pos[A[j]] means the new element A[j] is not in A[i+1..j-1], so it adds to the distinct count of A[i+1..j]). Then query the max value in the segment tree for i in [0, j-1]. Add R[j+1] to this max to get the candidate answer for this j.
Run the algorithm, track the maximum answer, and print it.
